transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex Chen: Okay we can see folks joining, hey everyone, thanks for pulling time together. I'm Alex, account exec on Redwood Inference. Priya's with me from the solutions team. Quick roll call?
[00:00:10] Dana Brooks: Dana here, CTO.
[00:00:13] Lena Ortiz: Lena, Head of ML.
[00:00:15] Samir Patel: Samir, security.
[00:00:18] Alex Chen: Great. High level agenda: scope the six week pilot, nail down success criteria, sizing and the security checklist — SOC 2, ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs and HIPAA specifics.
[00:00:32] Priya Raman: I'll jump into the technical pieces, especially the SSO and KMS flow and how we capture audit events in the console. Note: some transcribe is off in the doc so I'll clarify.
[00:00:45] Lena Ortiz: Perfect. Our immediate ask: we need to validate that Redwood can meet our compliance posture before we commit to a pilot — SOC 2 is table stakes, and we also need evidence of ISO27001 if possible. HIPAA is a hard requirement for PHI handling.
[00:01:01] Alex Chen: Understood. We can share a redacted SOC 2 Type II report and ISO cert — we'll also include a security whitepaper that covers encryption-at-rest, TLS in transit, KMS/HSM integrations, and network isolation options like VPC/private deployment.
[00:01:18] Samir Patel: How do you handle SSO? We run Okta and require SAML 2.0. Also RBAC: we need role separation so developers can't access production prompts or logs.
[00:01:28] Priya Raman: We support SAML SSO via SSO connector; can integrate with Okta. Our RBAC model supports roles at org, project, and route levels — you can restrict model deploys, viewing logs, and downloading tokens. I can send the role matrix.
[00:01:45] Samir Patel: And audit logs? Retention, integrity, access controls — we need tamper-evident logs for at least 2 years for a subset of events. Also exportability to our SIEM (Splunk).
[00:01:58] Priya Raman: Audit logs are streamed to a customer-owned cloud bucket or can be forwarded to your SIEM via syslog/HTTP. We sign logs and provide immutable append-only sequences; retention is configurable per customer. For pilot we usually enable 90 day retention, but we can export for long-term archival.
[00:02:14] Dana Brooks: HIPAA — do you offer a BAA?
[00:02:17] Alex Chen: We have a BAA template; coverage depends on deployment mode. For Private (VPC / on-prem) we can meet more restrictive reqs. Hosted can also be covered but will require contract addendum. We'll run legal review with your team.
[00:02:30] Lena Ortiz: On the pilot size: we're targeting an internal clinician assistant. For the pilot we'll route anonymized but realistic evidence. Expect about 50 concurrent inference requests at peak, avg 600 tokens per request, KV cache hit ~30%. Goal latency under 250ms p50 for typical prompts. Cost target TBD.
[00:02:50] Priya Raman: Important to capture session length distribution — that affects KV cache reuse and batching. Also, the 600 tokens average with 50 concurrency gives us a baseline for GPU selection and batch sizing. We'll propose a recommended pod size and quantization profile.
[00:03:06] Samir Patel: Benchmarks — we need a plan to validate latency and correctness. We want synthetic tests, and also a shadowing run where production traffic is mirrored to Redwood without affecting the user.
[00:03:18] Alex Chen: Agreed. Our standard benchmark plan for pilots: (1) synthetic latency/throughput sweep, (2) head-to-head with your on-prem baseline for 10k requests, (3) shadowing for 48-72 hours to collect fidelity metrics. We can also run cost-per-1k token estimates across model quantization choices.
[00:03:35] Lena Ortiz: Who owns the data in logs? We need to ensure PHI is not persisted in cleartext in hosted logs; also need to know what PII is redacted automatically.
[00:03:46] Priya Raman: For hosted, logs that include full prompt text are accessible only to customers via console; we encrypt at rest with your customer-managed KMS if you choose dedicated/private. We offer server-side PII redaction options and can mask prompts before persistence. For HIPAA pilot we recommend VPC + CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys).
[00:04:04] Samir Patel: Can you walk through the SAML setup and the flow for provisioning users and mapping roles?
[00:04:09] Priya Raman: Sure. Step 1: exchange metadata (IdP SAML metadata). Step 2: Redwood creates an SP entry and we map SAML attributes to roles (e.g., groups -> project:read, project:admin). Provisioning can be SCIM-enabled for automatic user provisioning.
[00:04:26] Lena Ortiz: We use Okta SCIM for provisioning, would be good. Also need to ensure least privilege for seeding teammates.
[00:04:31] Alex Chen: We'll include a simple sample config for Okta plus SCIM endpoints in the runbook.
[00:04:36] Dana Brooks: On timelines: We're aiming to start the pilot 2025-03-17 and run six weeks. That gives two weeks for legal and security review, one week for integration, then 3 weeks of active testing. Is that realistic?
[00:04:48] Priya Raman: Timeline is tight but doable if we get SOC 2 docs and the sizing worksheet fast. Integration for SAML + KMS typically takes 3-5 business days if Okta/SCIM is straightforward. Private deployment adds ~2 weeks for infra setup.
[00:05:03] Alex Chen: We'll mark dependencies: (A) SOC2/ISO artifacts delivered, (B) Nebula returns sizing worksheet, (C) Okta metadata and SCIM connect info, (D) legal BAA signoff. If those are met, target start 2025-03-17 is feasible.
[00:05:18] Samir Patel: A few deep technical Qs — how do you handle KV cache isolation across tenants? We can't have cross-tenant leakage.
[00:05:24] Priya Raman: KV caches are per-deployment and namespace-scoped. For hosted multi-tenant we use strong namespacing and encryption. Dedicated and private give physical isolation at the cluster level. We'll include cache isolation docs.
[00:05:38] Lena Ortiz: For benchmarks, we need to measure both cold-start and warm cache scenarios. Cold-start tail latencies are critical for clinician workflows.
[00:05:46] Priya Raman: We'll run tail-latency tests (p95, p99) and also run sequence-length stress tests. For the pilot we'll set SLOs: p50 < 250ms, p95 < 600ms as initial targets, subject to model selection.
[00:06:04] Samir Patel: Audit trail specifics: which events are captured? We need at minimum: auth events, model calls, admin changes, key rotations, and exports.
[00:06:12] Priya Raman: Our audit schema includes: user auth, token creates/deletes, model deploy/rollback, route changes, export/download, KMS key usage events, and retention changes. We can produce a sample event schema.
[00:06:25] Alex Chen: We'll also note that logs can be forwarded to Splunk and we provide a Kibana-like console for quick queries.
[00:06:31] Dana Brooks: Anything about data residency? Some of our researchers are in EU; we need a region for data processing.
[00:06:36] Priya Raman: We have region-based routing: EU region available for both hosted and dedicated. For pilot please specify region preference on the sizing worksheet.
[00:06:46] Lena Ortiz: On cost: give us rough ballpark per-1k tokens and a dedicated vs hosted delta. We'll need that for internal signoff.
[00:06:55] Alex Chen: We'll produce a cost estimate with model variants (fp16 vs 8-bit quantized) and expected token volumes. Typical hosted pilot costs for similar workloads have been X-20% lower than dedicated for low sustained usage, but dedicated wins at scale and for strict isolation. We'll share concrete numbers in the follow-up.
[00:07:10] Samir Patel: Encryption — when you say KMS integration, do you support customer-managed keys in AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault? What's the HSM story?
[00:07:18] Priya Raman: Yes, we support AWS KMS CMEK and Azure Key Vault; HSM-backed keys via Cloud HSM are supported for private deployments. We'll include the key rotation and access workflow in the runbook.
[00:07:31] Lena Ortiz: How do you handle prompt/response redaction in transit? We want PII removed before storing or shipping to third-party telemetry.
[00:07:39] Priya Raman: We have pre-save hooks that can mask or redact tokens with regex rules or an inline redaction service. For pilot we can provide a default regex set and work with your data team to tune it.
[00:07:51] Alex Chen: Let's capture acceptance criteria for the pilot so we have a pass/fail rubric. Proposed success criteria: (1) Security: SOC2 + BAA in place or legal signoff for hosted; SSO enabled and RBAC configured; audit logs flowing to Nebula SIEM. (2) Performance: p50 < 250ms, p95 < 600ms on selected model for 48h shadowing. (3) Quality: >= 90% of clinician prompt set judged acceptable on fidelity eval. (4) Ops: Runbook and playbooks in place, cost estimates validated.
[00:08:22] Dana Brooks: That sounds reasonable. On quality metric, we will provide the prompt set and scoring rubric.
[00:08:30] Alex Chen: Good. Any blockers?
[00:08:32] Samir Patel: Legal review of BAA is usually slow. We'll try to prioritize. Also, we need to see your SOC2 with auditor name redacted — some vendors redact too much and it becomes useless.
[00:08:45] Alex Chen: We'll send the redacted but auditor-identified copy and a short FAQ that explains what each control maps to.
[00:08:52] Lena Ortiz: Ok, last practical question: if we need private deployment, what's the onboarding lead time and what infra does Redwood need from us?
[00:08:59] Priya Raman: Private deployment typically needs: a VPC with peering, a set of subnets/GW, outbound NAT for image pulls, and optionally access to your KMS/HSM. Lead time is usually 2-3 weeks for small clusters, longer for air-gapped. We'll attach a checklist.
[00:09:16] Dana Brooks: Great, wrap up?
[00:09:18] Alex Chen: Quick recap and next steps: We'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts (Alex), sizing worksheet and cost estimate (Alex), SAML/SCIM runbook and KMS integration notes (Priya). Nebula team to return sizing worksheet and Okta metadata. Technical deep-dive tentatively 2025-03-11.
[00:09:36] Lena Ortiz: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[00:09:39] Samir Patel: Thanks.
[00:09:40] Priya Raman: Thanks all.
[00:09:42] Alex Chen: End call.
